findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed staff preparing drinks with bare hand contact of the food-contact surface of single-use plastic cups without proper handwashing occurring. Discussed with person-in-charge the need to wash hands frequently and/or avoid bare hand contact with any food-contact surfaces. Inspector observed these behaviors during an extremely busy rush which has been taken into consideration during the preparation of this report. However, it is during these rushes when the greatest number of consumers are served and the need for hand washing and avoiding bare-hand contact is most necessary. Discuss with staff the proper frequency for hand washing, even during such rushes, and the need to avoid any bare hand contact with the lips of cups where consumers place their mouths to drink to prevent hand-to-mouth contamination. Person-in-charge verified that the discussion would be held with staff and that the behavior will be corrected. Corrected-on-site. No follow-up required. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Wiping cloths (bar rags) must be stored in sanitizer when not actively being used. These rags may never be stored on countertops or other surfaces during food (drink) service. Wet rags allow bacterial growth to occur rapidly in the rags which are then used to wipe surfaces. These rags are also handled by staff members who were not washing hands frequently during service and then touching the lips of single-service cups used to serve customers. Any bacteria or other pathogens present on these rags are then transferred to the lips of cups. This contamination is a source of foodborne illness. Ensure that wet wiping cloths (rags) are stored properly in sanitizer which has been tested to ensure proper concentration of chemical sanitizer in the solution. Inspector discussed this requirement with person-in-charge who confirmed understanding and assured future compliance with this requirement. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
During the busy rush at the bar, inspector observed several instances of staff members tossing the ice scoop into the ice bin without consideration for how the handle landed in the ice. This behavior results in staff members reaching into the ice bin and touching the ice with bare hands. As discussed previously, other inappropriate behaviors contribute to contaminated hands which are then potentially touching ice which is used for drink service. Ensure that ice scoops are stored with the handle up at all times and that bare hand contact with ice is prevented at all times. Discussed with person-in-charge who assured inspector that these behaviors will be corrected. Corrected-on-site. No follow-up required. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed a plastic glass in the bottom of the cabinet under the popcorn machine storing oil for the popcorn machine. Provide a handled scoop for the oil.

750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed wine glasses stored on a white cloth towel in the front bar area. Provide a mat or material down for glasses.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed a box of cups stored on the floor in the back storage area. Move the cups up 6 inches up off the floor.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed doors in the back bar area with gaps at the bottom and on the side of the South door. Observed the main door to have a gap at the bottom of it. Seal and replace weather stripping on the doors. Make them where light cannot be seen thru.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Wall inside the walkin cooler with areas where draft beer lines had been run. The have foam in them and are not easily cleanable. Cover the holes and make easily cleanable.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed a can of insecticide on top of some Red Bull in the back storage area. (Corrected) Worker removed the spray and put it with the other chemicals. (Corrected)
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.
